title: US announces Operation Prosperity Guardian to protect Red Sea shipping
body:
On 18 December 2023, US Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin announced Operation Prosperity Guardian, an international maritime security initiative to counter Houthi attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea. The Houthis, a Yemeni movement controlling much of the north and west of the country, had begun attacking vessels after the Gaza war broke out in October 2023, saying they were acting in support of Palestinians.

The initiative was led by the United States and operated under Combined Task Force 153 of the Combined Maritime Forces. Contributors listed included the United Kingdom, Australia, Bahrain, Canada, Denmark, Finland, Greece, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Singapore and Sri Lanka, with Seychelles offering support without ships or personnel. France, Italy and Spain declined to take part under the US-led command, and Egypt and Saudi Arabia were absent.

By 1 January 2024, at least 17 civilian vessels had been attacked. On 10 January 2024, the Houthis launched their largest barrage, 18 to 24 drones and missiles, and the coalition conducted its first airstrikes in Yemen two days later. Six of the ten largest container shipping companies were largely avoiding the Red Sea, according to the article, and daily transits of bulk carriers and tankers fell in early January 2024.
